_README: Hand resolutions for the Dataroma superinvestor roster, read by fetch_superinvestors.load_superinvestor_overrides.
cik_overrides: Dataroma code -> 13F-manager CIK for the names EDGAR company search gets wrong or cannot see. A hand mapping always wins over a stored or EDGAR resolution.

Most failures are mutual-fund SHARE CLASSES whose 13F filer is the ADVISER, not the fund, so the fund name never filed a 13F-HR; re-querying on the adviser name resolves them. Naive auto-resolution gets only 12 of the 23 managers Dataroma has dropped since 2013 (52%), and misses 16 more that are on the roster today.

AMBIGUITY IS SETTLED BY 13F ROW COUNT IN sec13f_hr, never by name alone: lmvtx had 2 candidates (14,379 rows vs 809), oakvx 3 (1,233 vs 1 vs 1), FPACX/FPPTX 3 (2,271 vs 0 vs 0) and pzfvx 2 (2,789 vs 0). A name match that filed nothing is not the manager: First Pacific Advisors INC (0 rows) is not the LLC that files.
unresolvable: the codes allowed to resolve to no CIK, each with its reason. Their rows are still written (cik NULL, resolution='unresolved') so they stay visible; any other unresolved code raises.
Both entries are unresolvable for the same measured reason: the EDGAR company search filters on type=13F-HR, and neither entity ever filed one (HTTP 200, zero <company-info> blocks).
